extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Approval and effect of an Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, leading to exclusion on consent from practice before the USPTO in trademark and other non-patent matters, and related procedural obligations. Covers required acknowledgments, alleged misconduct types, regulatory violations cited, publication and reinstatement consequences, and post-order procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will approve an Affidavit of Resignation only if it 'complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).' The affidavit is submitted for the purpose of being excluded on consent pursuant to § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the Director determined the Affidavit 'complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)' and therefore approved it; compliance triggers approval and exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary consent (no coercion or duress)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge that his consent is 'freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit must explicitly state voluntariness; this is a prerequisite for approving exclusion on consent under § 11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of pending disciplinary complaint and specific allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge he is aware a disciplinary complaint is pending and acknowledge the nature of the allegations against him (listed in the affidavit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit enumerates alleged facts (e.g., not authorized to practice patent law, formation/control of The Inventors Network, permitting unlicensed filing/prosecution of >150 patent applications, misrepresentations to applicants and the Office). Awareness and acknowledgment of these allegations are required elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of specific alleged wrongful acts (unauthorized practice and related misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit details alleged acts including: forming/controlling The Inventors Network; permitting filing/prosecution of over 150 patent applications without involvement of a registered patent practitioner; charging fees representing that a registered practitioner would handle matters; failing to disburse fees to registered practitioners; preparing/signing documents in a registered practitioner's name; providing patent legal services and prosecution without being licensed; misrepresenting himself as a registered practitioner (including participating in telephone conferences with USPTO Examiners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factual allegations function as the operative misconduct claims that the respondent acknowledges awareness of; although respondent did not admit the allegations, he consents that they will be presumed true for reinstatement purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscribed misconduct under USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint alleges violations of Disciplinary Rules including: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) (disreputable or gross conduct); § 10.23(b)(4) (dishonesty, fraud, deceit, misrepresentation); § 10.23(b)(5) (conduct prejudicial to administration of justice); § 10.31(a) (misleading advertising); § 10.23(b)(3) (illegal conduct involving moral turpitude, by acts constituting violations of 35 U.S.C. § 33); § 10.23(b)(6) (other conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice); and § 10.89(c)(6) (intentional or habitual violation of the Disciplinary Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists the specific regulatory provisions alleged to have been violated; these are the disciplinary standards used to assess fitness and misconduct before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's statutory and regulatory authority to approve and exclude
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's authority to approve an affidavit of resignation and to exclude on consent is grounded in 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly cites the statutory/regulatory basis for approving exclusions on consent—this is the legal standard authorizing the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of consenting to exclusion: exclusion from practice in specified matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Once approved, the respondent 'shall be excluded on consent from the practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters' effective on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit's approval results in immediate exclusion from specific areas of practice before the USPTO as stated in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirements for Final Order and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires public posting (Reading Room URL) and Official Gazette notice summarizing the facts and regulatory bases; the Order provides model language for the Gazette notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption on reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (i) the allegations in the disciplinary complaint are true and (ii) he could not have successfully defended himself against such allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent to exclusion carries a specific, binding evidentiary presumption affecting future reinstatement proceedings; applicants must understand this consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order imposes ongoing regulatory obligations referenced by citation; § 11.58 governs scope/effect of exclusion and related duties (order requires respondent to adhere to that rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director 'shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires the OED Director to follow the publication/processing/notice procedures set out in § 11.59 when approving an affidavit of resignation and exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations on reinstatement: compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent 'shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order makes clear that reinstatement requests are governed by § 11.60, including the consequences and presumptions described therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement to jointly move to dismiss pending disciplinary complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall 'jointly move the hearing officer to dismiss the pending disciplinary complaint within 14 days of the date of this Final Order.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval of the affidavit and exclusion on consent is accompanied by a timely joint-motion obligation to dismiss the underlying complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent 'shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies that each party is responsible for its own costs related to the disciplinary matter and implementation of the agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order states exclusion is effective 'beginning on the date this Final Order is signed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion-on-consent takes effect immediately upon the Director's signature on the Final Order; timing matters for compliance and notification.
